actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

facts.text: The release packages nine G1 simulation environments and MuJoCo assets
The project requires Linux and Python 3.10; an NVIDIA GPU and CUDA are needed only for WBC execution or EGL rendering, and recorded playback can run CPU-only
MuJoCo is pinned to 3.2.6 and RoboSuite to 1.5.1
The package requires Python 3.10 or newer and declares mujoco==3.2.6, numpy==1.26.4, robosuite==1.5.1 and robosuite-models==1.0.0 as dependencies
The card's primary model is the MJCF robot named g1_29dof_with_hand_rev_1_0 with angle unit radian
The robot is attached to the world by a free joint named base on the root body
The actuator block declares 29 motor actuators
The twelve leg motors have control ranges -88 to 88 for hip pitch and hip yaw, -139 to 139 for hip roll and knee, and -50 to 50 for ankle pitch and ankle roll
The three waist motors have control ranges -88 to 88 (yaw), -50 to 50 (roll) and -50 to 50 (pitch)
The fourteen arm motors have control ranges -25 to 25 for shoulder pitch, shoulder roll, shoulder yaw and elbow, -30 to 30 for wrist roll, and -10 to 10 for wrist pitch and wrist yaw
The model declares four IMU sensors: a gyroscope and an accelerometer on the torso site and another pair on the pelvis site
The asset section references 33 mesh STL files under meshes/
The G1 robot class is a RoboSuite LeggedManipulatorModel
The G1 constructor loads robots/unitree_g1/g1_29dof_rev_1_0.xml
The left three-finger hand is a separate MJCF model named g1_threefinger_left_hand
The left hand MJCF declares seven position actuators
The right three-finger hand is a separate MJCF model named g1_threefinger_right_hand
The right hand MJCF declares seven position actuators
The left hand gripper loads g1_threefinger_left_hand.xml
The right hand gripper loads g1_threefinger_right_hand.xml
LocoManipulationEnv is a RoboSuite ManipulationEnv
GroundOnly is a pass-through subclass of LocoManipulationEnv
LMSimpleEnv selects GroundArena as its arena
GroundArena loads arenas/ground_arena.xml
The ground arena MJCF holds the floor plane and four fixed cameras (frontview, birdview, agentview, sideview)

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates the loaded MJCF deterministically from the reset state and the model has no random element; the bridge takes no seed and a reset restores the model defaults.  The package's fake is deterministic too, but its placeholder motion is not the engine's physics.

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it parses the card's MJCF for one free joint and 29 hinge joints (36 qpos, 35 dof), the 29 motor actuators and their ctrlranges, then moves each actuated hinge a placeholder fraction toward its control value; it computes no inertias, contacts, friction, actuator or sensor dynamics and was never compared with the engine
the model file sets no <option timestep>; the published timestep_ms is MuJoCo's library default (0.002 s) supplied by the fake's fallback, not a value stated by the model

models[0] is a robot asset, not a full scene: it has one free-floating base and no floor, arena or camera.  The upstream environments compose it with a separate ground arena (GroundArena loads arenas/ground_arena.xml), so the bare model falls under gravity in the real engine

the three-finger hands are separate MJCF fragments attached by the upstream environment as grippers; the loaded model has 29 body actuators and no hand joints, so the seven position actuators of each hand are not part of this world

the stand-in loads no mesh or texture (the model's asset section names 33 STL files) and resolves no contact, tendon or equality constraint; a real engine load needs the meshes beside the model, which the pinned clone provides
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by the model step only
no rendering, cameras or sensor publication: the four IMU sensors of the model are not exposed; the observation is only the bridge's time, qpos, qvel and ctrl
the card's five entry symbols are RoboSuite environments; they are not imported or run, and their task, object, randomization and success logic is not modelled
MuJoCo itself was not installed where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine; no physical G1 is modelled and nothing was validated against the robot

measures.description: Simulated time since the last reset
measures.name: time_ms

measures.description: Control vector last applied to the actuators (ctrl)
measures.name: ctrl

measures.description: Integration steps since the last reset
measures.name: tick

measures.description: Integration step of the model (null when the model states none)
measures.name: timestep_ms

measures.description: Seed the bridge was configured with
measures.name: seed

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.
measures.name: native_checkpoint

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: after an e-stop no step or reset is accepted until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the integration state is kept and stays readable
